units.en: Have you ever wanted to write a story but wondered where to start?
units.zh: 你有没有想过写一个故事，但想知道从哪里开始？

units.en: The Write Your Own Story Book is here to help.
units.zh: 写你自己的故事书是为了帮助。

units.en: It's full of inspiring ideas for all kinds of different stories, with space for you to write them in, and writing tips to help you on your way.
units.zh: 它充满了对各种不同故事的鼓舞人心的想法，有空间供您编写，并撰写提示以帮助您继续前进。

units.zh: 用可持续来源的纸制成

units.zh: 在这本书中，你会找到很多空间来写你自己的故事，以及帮助你成为一个了不起的作者的想法和建议。

units.en: You can start writing right away, or you could turn to the 'Story Writing Toolkit' on pages 82-95 to find some help, with general writing tips and checklists.
units.zh: 您可以立即开始写作，也可以翻阅第 82-95 页的“故事写作工具包”以寻求帮助，以及一般写作技巧和清单。

units.zh: 这里有故事建议，在您计划时要问自己的问题

You could choose characters, settings and actions from the lists on these pages or invent some of your own.

units.en: All stories need a beginning, a middle and an end.
units.zh: 所有故事都需要开头、中段和结尾。

units.en: Something goes wrong - a mystery, a dramatic event or a disagreement.
units.zh: 出了岔子：可能出现了一个谜团、一件突发大事，或一场争执。

units.en: Before you start writing a story, it's a good idea to plan an outline of what's going to happen in each part.
units.zh: 开始写故事之前，最好先列一个提纲，想好每一部分会发生什么。

units.en: happens to your characters to start the action.
units.zh: 发生在你的角色开始动作。

units.zh: 这样做的一种方法是将您的故事视为一座山，如下所示：

units.en: The threads of the story are tied up.
units.zh: 故事的线索被捆绑在一起。

units.en: Introduce your characters and the setting.

units.zh: 现在写一个短篇小说的大纲。

units.zh: 按照您的大纲在此页面上写下您的故事。
在这里写下你的故事标题。

units.en: When you come to plan the outine for a longer story, you might
units.zh: 当你来计划一个更长的故事时，你可能会

units.en: want your character to face more than one problem.
units.zh: 希望您的角色面临不止一种问题。

units.en: Jo your story mountain may have several peaks.
units.zh: 乔你的故事山可能有几座山峰。

units.en: When you write a story, it's your job to create interesting, believable characters who will capture the reader's imagination.
units.zh: 当你写一个故事时，你的工作是创造有趣、可信的角色，这些角色将捕捉读者的想象力。

units.en: You don't have to tell the reader everything about your characters, but the more you know about them the more convincing they'll be.
units.zh: 你不必告诉读者你的角色的一切，但你对他们的了解越多，他们就会越有说服力。

units.en: Who or what is he, she or it?
To start building up a character, fill in this diagram with words describing him or her.
units.zh: 要开始构建角色，请用描述他或她的文字填写此图。

units.en: Once you've decided what your character is like, it's what he or she says and does in different situations that helps to drive a story.
units.zh: 一旦你决定了你的角色是什么样的，这就是他或她在不同的情况下所说和所做的事情，这有助于推动故事。

units.en: Imagine it's the strangest, most wonderful day of your character's life and write a short story about it.
units.zh: 想象一下，这是你角色一生中最奇怪、最美妙的一天，并写一个关于它的短篇小说。

units.en: The best way to bring your character
units.zh: 带来你的性格的最佳方式

units.en: to life is to describe how he or she acts.
units.zh: 生活就是描述他或她的行为方式。

units.en: For example, you don't need to say a character is generous if you show him doing or saying something generous.
units.zh: 例如，如果你展示他在做或说一些慷慨的事情，你不需要说一个角色是慷慨的。

units.en: You can find more help with building
units.zh: 您可以在构建方面找到更多帮助

units.en: Whether you set your story in the real world, or a fantasy kingdom, on board a pirate ship or in a toy store, you can make it more vivid by describing the setting in detail.
units.zh: 无论您是在现实世界中，还是在海盗船上或在玩具商店中设置您的故事，您都可以通过详细描述设置来使其更加生动。

units.en: To help you flex your descriptive muscles, write a letter describing your home to someone who is coming to stay for the first time.
units.zh: 为了帮助您锻炼描述性肌肉，写一封信，向第一次来的人写一封描述您的家的信。

units.en: Imagine your guest comes from a foreign land - maybe even another world.
units.zh: 想象一下你的客人来自异国他乡——甚至可能是另一个世界。

units.en: It may all be familiar to you, but what would it look, sound, feel and smell like to a stranger?
units.zh: 这对你来说可能都很熟悉，但对陌生人来说，它看起来、声音、感觉和闻起来会是什么样子？

units.en: Do you have any unusual objects or customs at home that might need to be explained to an outsider?
units.zh: 您家中是否有任何不寻常的物品或习俗可能需要向外人解释？

units.en: One way to get inside the head of a character is to write as though he or she is telling a story about him- or herself, perhaps in a letter or a diary.
units.zh: 进入角色头脑的一种方法是写作，就好像他或她正在讲述一个关于他或她自己的故事，也许是在信或日记中。

units.en: This means that - instead of writing about the character as "he" or
units.zh: 这意味着 - 而不是将角色写成“他”或

units.en: "she" - you write from the "I' point of view.
Fill in this journal to tell the story of a character's first week at a new school.
units.zh: 填写这本日记，讲述一个角色在新学校的第一周的故事。

units.en: • What kind of school is it?
• How is it different from your character's previous school?
units.zh: • 它与您角色以前的学校有何不同？

units.en: • Does he or she join any clubs?
units.zh: • 他或她是否加入任何俱乐部？

units.en: • Who does your character think he or she will be friends with?
units.zh: • 你的角色认为他或她会和谁成为朋友？

units.en: • Is there anyone he or she doesn't like?
units.zh: • 有没有他或她不喜欢的人？

units.en: • Does he or she get into trouble?
• Is there anything next weck that your character is looking forward to, or dreading?
units.zh: • 你的角色接下来有什么期待或害怕的事情吗？

units.en: Library nervous uniform worst enemy late for class
units.zh: 图书馆神经制服最坏的敌人上课迟到
在这里写下你的故事标题。

units.en: A story can turn out very differently depending on which character you choose to focus on.
units.zh: 根据您选择关注的角色，故事的结果可能非常不同。

units.en: Usually, Cinderella is told from her point of view.
units.zh: 通常，从她的角度讲述灰姑娘。

units.en: But what if someone else took the spotlight?
units.zh: 但是，如果其他人成为焦点呢？

units.en: Try retelling the story from the point of view of one of these characters instead:
units.zh: 尝试从以下角色之一的角度重述故事：

units.en: • What do the other characters think of Cinderella?
units.zh: • 其他角色对灰姑娘的看法？

units.en: • Did the original story get it right?
• How does your character feel at the end of the story?
units.zh: • 你的角色在故事的结尾感觉如何？

units.en: 1. Cinderella lives with her father, her stepmother and her two ugly stepsisters.
units.zh: 1. 灰姑娘和她的父亲、她的继母和两个丑陋的继姐妹住在一起。

units.en: 3. The stepsisters go off to a ball, but Cinderella has nothing to wear and stays at home.
units.zh: 3. 继姐妹们去参加一个球，但灰姑娘没有什么可穿的，留在家里。

units.en: 4. Luckily, she has a Fairy Godmother who conjures up a ball dress and a coach out of rags and a pumpkin.
units.zh: 4. 幸运的是，她有一个仙女教母，她用破布和南瓜换了一件球衣和一个教练。

units.en: 5. Cinderella CAN go to the ball - but only until midnight, when her finery will turn back into rags.
units.zh: 5. 灰姑娘可以去球——但直到午夜，她的服饰会变成破布。

units.en: 6. At the ball, Cinderella dances with Prince
units.zh: 6.在舞会上，灰姑娘与王子共舞

units.en: Charming and they fall in love.
Cinderella runs away, but loses a shoe.
units.zh: 灰姑娘跑了，但失去了鞋子。

units.en: 8. Prince Charming picks up the shoe.
He swears to marry the girl whose foot it fits, and searches the kingdom for her.
units.zh: 他发誓要嫁给它适合脚的女孩，并在王国中寻找她。

units.en: 9. I he ugly sisters try on the shoe.
It doesn't fit them but it does fit Cinderella.
units.zh: 它不适合它们，但它确实适合灰姑娘。

units.en: 10. Cinderella marries the prince and they live happily ever after - or do they?
units.zh: 10. 灰姑娘嫁给了王子，他们从此过上了幸福的生活——或者是吗？

units.en: When you tell a story from a particular character's point of view, you can only write about things your character has seen or heard.
units.zh: 当你从特定角色的角度讲故事时，你只能写出你的角色所看到或听到的东西。

units.en: • include things he or she couldn't know, " it makes the story less believable.
units.zh: • 包括他或她不知道的事情，“这让故事变得不那么可信。

units.en: You flip through the pages and find that someone has started to write a story in it.
units.zh: 你翻阅页面，发现有人开始在其中写故事。

units.en: It's up to you to finish it.
Billy clung onto the rail of the ship as the vessel tipped this way and that.
units.zh: 当船倾倒在这条路上时，比利紧紧抓住船的轨道。

units.en: It was the worst storm hed ever seen.
units.zh: 这是他见过的最严重的风暴。

units.en: With one powerful lurch, he felt himself being Thrown across the deck.
units.zh: 一股强大的低潮，他感到自己被扔到了甲板上。

units.en: Winded and terrified, he looked up as a flash of Lightning lit up the ocean.
units.zh: 他惊恐地惊恐地抬起头，一道闪电照亮了大海。

units.en: Questions to ask yourself before you start
units.zh: 在开始之前问自己的问题

units.en: Just ahead of the ship's bow, he saw...
units.zh: 就在船头的前方，他看到了……

units.en: • Why is Billy on the ship?
• What kind of ship is it a navy vessel, a pleasure cruiser, a pirate ship?
units.zh: • 它是什么样的船，是海军舰艇、游船、海盗船？

units.en: Is it going to get there?
• How does Billy try to overcome the danger?
units.zh: • 比利如何试图克服危险？

units.en: • Does anyone or anything get in his way?
units.zh: • 有人或任何事妨碍他吗？

units.en: Speaking parts parts) will help bring your readers right into the action.
units.zh: 说话零件部分）将帮助您的读者直接参与行动。

units.en: This is usually shown in quotation marks like this.
units.zh: 这通常在这样的引号中显示。

units.en: "He's catching up with us," panted Nathan.

units.zh: 每一幅图都讲着一个故事

units.en: Write a story about the picture on the right.
units.zh: 写一个关于右边图片的故事。

units.en: You could write about the whole scene, or just one part that catches your attention.
units.zh: 你可以写整个场景，或者只是引起你注意的一部分。

units.en: You could even choose to write about something that's just out of sight.
units.zh: 你甚至可以选择写一些看不见的东西。

units.en: Is it in a huge mansion or a tiny bungalow?
units.zh: 是在大豪宅还是小平房里？

units.en: In the countryside or at the edge of a big city?
units.zh: 在乡下还是在大城市的边缘？

units.en: • Who is the man outside the window and what is he doing?
units.zh: • 窗外的人是谁，他在做什么？

units.en: • What's beyond the mountains in the distance?
units.zh: • 远处的山脉之外有什么？

units.en: • What are the mice up to?
• Where does the archway behind the bookshelves lead?
units.zh: • 书架后面的拱门通向哪里？

units.en: • Who's the woman in the painting?
• Who does the crystal ball on the table belong to?
units.zh: • 桌子上的水晶球属于谁？

units.en: Once upon a time... that's how all fairy tales begin.
units.zh: 曾几何时……这就是所有童话故事的开始。

units.en: But now you can decide how the story goes, using the lists on these pages to help you.
units.zh: 但是现在您可以使用这些页面上的列表来决定故事的进展情况来帮助您。
• 有一个意想不到的客人
从此以后快乐地生活着

units.en: Here's an unfinished comic strip about two young pirates going on an exciting treasure hunt.
units.zh: 这是一部未完成的漫画，讲述了两名年轻的海盗进行激动人心的寻宝活动。

units.en: The pictures have been drawn, but what are the characters saying?
units.zh: 图片已经画了，但人物在说什么？

units.en: Now it's up to you to tell the story by writing dialogue in the speech bubbles.
units.zh: 现在轮到你来讲这个故事了：在对话气泡里写出人物的对白。

units.en: Imagine it's possible to travel through time.
units.zh: 想象一下，穿越时空是可能的。

units.en: Choose a time and a place that excites you and write a story about a journey to that time.
units.zh: 选择一个让你兴奋的时间和地点，写一个关于那个时代的旅程的故事。

units.en: • Who travels through time and how?
units.zh: • 谁穿越时间以及如何穿越？

units.en: Or using some sort of time machine?
units.zh: 还是使用某种时间机器？

units.en: If so, what happens if it breaks down?
units.zh: 如果是这样，如果它坏了怎么办？

units.en: • Where do your characters travel to and when?
units.zh: • 您的角色何时前往何处？

units.en: • Do they plan to solve a mystery, to bring back future technology or to try to change the course of history?
units.zh: • 他们打算解开一个谜团，带回未来的技术还是试图改变历史进程？

units.en: • What problems and dangers do they come across?
units.zh: • 他们遇到了哪些问题和危险？

units.en: • If your story's set in the past, do the characters meet any historical figures?
units.zh: • 如果您的故事是过去的，这些角色是否遇到了任何历史人物？

units.en: • How do people live, dress and get around in the time youre writing about?
units.zh: • 在您写作的时间里，人们如何生活、穿着和出行？

units.en: • Do your characters travel back to their own time in the end?
units.zh: • 你的角色最终会回到自己的时间吗？

units.en: Here are a few times and places you could write about:
units.zh: 以下是您可以写的几次和地方：

units.en: Historical or futuristic details about how people live - such as what their homes look like, how they communicate or what they eat - will help make your story vivid.
units.zh: 关于人们生活方式的历史或未来细节——例如他们的家是什么样子、他们如何交流或吃什么——将有助于让你的故事生动。

units.en: But don't spend too long describing the setting - what happens to the characters is much more important.
units.zh: 但不要花太长时间描述设置 - 角色会发生什么更重要。

units.en: Imagine your family suddenly inherits lots of money from a long-lost uncle, and you become instant millionaires.
units.zh: 想象一下，你的家人突然从一个失散多年的叔叔那里继承了很多钱，你就变成了百万富翁。

units.en: But there's a catch - you also inherit something else.
units.zh: 但是有一个问题——你还继承了别的东西。

units.en: Something that turns your lives upside down.
units.zh: 让你的生活颠倒过来的东西。

units.en: (It's up to you to decide what that is.)
• What's the first thing you buy with your new-found fortune?
units.zh: • 你用新发现的财富买的第一件东西是什么？

units.en: • Does your family fight about how to divide the money?
units.zh: • 您的家人是否为如何划分钱而争吵？

units.en: A letter containing a family secret?
units.zh: 一封包含家庭秘密的信？
令人毛骨悚然的老房子？
争吵的开玩笑的沙发不和竞争

units.en: step father show off nagging revelation secret suspicion
units.zh: 继父炫耀启示的秘密怀疑

units.en: Write a story about a character who has an amazing power.
units.zh: 写一个关于具有惊人力量的角色的故事。

units.en: But make sure your character has a weakness or two and a powerful enemy to defeat.
units.zh: 但要确保你的角色有一两个弱点和一个强大的敌人要击败。

units.en: If everything's too easy, the story could get boring.
units.zh: 如果一切都太简单了，故事可能会变得无聊。

units.en: • the ability to control the weather
• telekinesis (can move objects without touching them)
units.zh: • 心灵感应（可以在不触摸物体的情况下移动物体）

units.en: • How does your character get her or his powers?
units.zh: • 你的角色如何获得她或他的力量？

units.en: • Are there any downsides to having them?
units.zh: • 拥有它们有什么缺点吗？

units.en: • What does she or he use them for?
• Does your character's enemy have powers too?
units.zh: • 你角色的敌人也有力量吗？

units.en: • What is your character's main goal?
units.zh: • 你的角色的主要目标是什么？

units.en: Does he or she achieve it?
When you're describing the action, think of strong, exciting verbs (doing words) to make it more dramatic.
units.zh: 当你描述动作时，想想强有力的、令人兴奋的动词（做词）以使其更具戏剧性。

units.en: For example, instead of writing, she jumped you could say, "she leaped," and instead of, "he ran fast," the sprinted," might sound more dynamic.
units.zh: 例如，她跳跃而不是写作，你可以说，“她跳了”，而不是“他跑得快”，冲刺，可能听起来更有活力。

units.en: When you're bringing your story to a close, try to include a final confrontation between your character and his or her main enemy.
units.zh: 当你结束你的故事时，试着包括你的角色和他或她的主要敌人之间的最后对抗。

units.en: You could set this somewhere dramatic, such as the villain's lair.
units.zh: 你可以把它设置在一个戏剧性的地方，比如反派的巢穴。

units.en: Write about a group of animals who live in a forest.
units.zh: 写下一群住在森林里的动物。

units.en: One day they learn that humans are going to clear the trees and build a shopping mall.
units.zh: 有一天，他们了解到人类将清理树木并建造购物中心。

units.en: • What kind of animals are they?
Are they a family of the same species, or sworn
units.zh: 它们是同一物种的家族，还是宣誓

units.en: enemies who are forced to work together?
Does it have tall trees to climb or thick undergrowth to hide in?

units.en: Wherever you go, make a note of the sights and sounds that interest you
units.zh: 无论您走到哪里，都要记下您感兴趣的景点和声音

units.en: You never know when you might stumble upon the setting
units.zh: 你永远不知道什么时候你会偶然发现这个场景

units.en: When it comes to writing, it's not enough to have a gripping plot, believable characters or an atmospheric setting - the words you use to describe them make a big difference to how enjoyable your story is to read.
units.zh: 在写作方面，仅仅有一个扣人心弦的情节、可信的人物或大气的环境是不够的——你用来描述它们的词语对你的故事阅读的乐趣有很大的不同。

units.en: So try to think of interesting adjectives (describing words) and verbs (action words).
units.zh: 所以试着想想有趣的形容词（描述词）和动词（动作词）。

units.en: You might say a beautiful princess was.
units.zh: 你可能会说一个美丽的公主是。

units.en: Common adjectives include big, small, ugly, beautiful, bad and good.
units.zh: 常见的形容词包括大、小、丑、美、坏和好。

units.en: But there are so many others to choose from, make sure you don't always use the same ones.
units.zh: 但是还有很多其他的可供选择，请确保您不会总是使用相同的。
一场激动人心的冒险可能是...

units.en: An Egyptian tomb could be described as...
units.zh: 一座埃及坟墓可以说是...

units.en: My love is like a red, red rose...
units.zh: 我的爱就像一朵红红的玫瑰……

units.en: To give a clearer picture of the thing you're describing, you could compare it to something else.
units.zh: 为了更清楚地了解您所描述的内容，您可以将其与其他内容进行比较。

units.en: So you might say, "a monster is as tall as a skyscraper," or "a fairy's voice tinkles like a bell."
units.zh: 所以你可能会说，“一个怪物像摩天大楼一样高”，或者“仙女的声音像铃铛一样叮当作响。”

units.en: This kind of comparison is known as a simile.
Try witing of some of your own here.
units.zh: 在这里尝试一些你自己的。

units.en: These tell you what a character or thing does, thinks or feels and can reflect a person's mood or personality.
units.zh: 这些告诉你一个角色或事物的作用、想法或感受，以及可以反映一个人的情绪或个性。
当我和我的朋友在一起时，...

units.en: When I'm in a hurry, I...
Adverbs are words which describe verbs - for example,
units.zh: 副词是描述动词的词——例如，

units.en: • But adverbs can make your witing sound clumsy.
units.zh: • 但副词会让你的智慧听起来很笨拙。

units.en: If you use more interesting verbs, you can avoid using adverbs altogether, and say what you mean more concisely.
units.zh: 如果你使用更多有趣的动词，你可以完全避免使用副词，并更简洁地说出你的意思。

units.en: For example, instead of, "She stood up quickly from her seat and shouted loudy" you could say, "She sprang from her seat and bellowed."
units.zh: 例如，你可以说，“她从座位上站起来，大喊大叫”，而不是“她从座位上跳起来，吼道。”

units.en: If you want to add richer detail and greater depth to your writing, you could try using different styles and points of view to see
units.zh: 如果你想为你的写作添加更丰富的细节和更深的深度，你可以尝试使用不同的风格和观点来查看

units.en: Experiment with your sentences You can tell the same story many different ways.
units.zh: 尝试你的句子，你可以以多种不同的方式讲述同一个故事。

units.en: For example, you could write: The boy ran along the street.
units.zh: 例如，你可以写：男孩沿着街跑。

units.en: He was being chased by a tiger.
but you could also write: Panting for breath, the boy raced along the street.
units.zh: 但你也可以写：喘着粗气，男孩沿着街道奔跑。

units.en: The tiger was getting close: or you could put it like this:
units.zh: 老虎越来越近了：或者你可以这样说：

units.en: There's get at me ning as Fast
Adding speech, like this, helps to bring drama to your stories, and makes your characters more convincing.
units.zh: 像这样添加语音有助于为您的故事带来戏剧性，并使您的角色更有说服力。

units.en: Whether you choose to write in the past or present tense can make a big difference to the impact of your story.
units.zh: 无论您选择用过去还是现在时写作，都会对故事的影响产生重大影响。

units.en: Most stories are written in the past tense, because it's usually what comes most naturally: Once, upon a time, there were three bears.
units.zh: 大多数故事都是用过去时写的，因为它通常是最自然的：曾经，一段时间，有三只熊。

units.en: But the present tense can be useful, especially if you want to draw your readers into the action - as though it's taking place right in front of them:
units.zh: 但是现在时可能很有用，特别是如果你想把你的读者吸引到动作中——就好像它发生在他们面前一样：

units.en: So I'm walking down the road, minding my own
units.zh: 所以我走在路上，想着自己

units.en: business when all of a sudden...
Your story will become confusing if you switch from one tense to another.
units.zh: 如果您从一种时态切换到另一种时态，您的故事将变得令人困惑。

units.en: It's best to choose one and stick to it.
units.zh: 最好选择一种并坚持下去。

units.en: The 'voice' you use to tell a story is known as the narrator.
units.zh: 你用来讲故事的“声音”被称为叙述者。

units.en: You can achieve different effects depending on the point
units.zh: 您可以根据点获得不同的效果

units.en: of view you choose for your narrator.
units.zh: 您为叙述者选择的视图。
“我/我们”的观点 = 第一人称：

units.en: When I woke up this moring,
I had no idea what adventures
This point of view helps to make a story seem personal, as though it's being told by someone involved in the events.
units.zh: 这种观点有助于使故事看起来像个人，就好像它是由参与事件的人讲述的那样。

units.en: You know you're in trouble when the boss gives you
units.zh: 当老板给你时，你知道你有麻烦

units.en: The narrator may not know the whole story, and can only talk about what he or she knows.
units.zh: 叙述者可能不知道整个故事，只能谈论他或她所知道的。

units.en: This is an unusual point of view, but it can be an effective way of bringing the reader closer to the narrator, as though they are both in it together.
units.zh: 这是一个不寻常的观点，但它可以成为让读者更接近叙述者的有效方式，就好像他们俩在一起一样。

units.en: A burly figure strode across the deck, his crimson frockcoat flapping in the sea breeze.
units.zh: 一个身材魁梧的身影大步穿过甲板，他的深红色连衣裙在海风中飘扬。

units.en: Where his left hand should have
units.zh: 他的左手应该有的地方

units.en: Here, the narrator describes a scene almost as though he or she is watching a movie.
units.zh: 在这里，叙述者描述了一个场景，就像他或她正在看电影一样。

units.en: This is the point of view writers use most often.
units.zh: 这是作者最常使用的观点。

units.en: It allows you to get inside the mind of more than one character and gives your readers a chance to see the story from different angles.
units.zh: 它使您可以进入多个角色的思想，并让您的读者有机会从不同的角度观看故事。

units.en: If you want to give your imagination a work-out, you could try writing micro-stories.
units.zh: 如果你想发挥你的想象力，你可以尝试写微故事。

units.en: These should have a beginning, a middle and an end, just as longer stories do.
units.zh: 这些应该有一个开始，一个中间和一个结束，就像更长的故事一样。

units.en: The only difference is that they should be short enough to fit on a single piece of paper or in a text message.
units.zh: 唯一的区别是它们应该足够短，可以放在一张纸或短信中。

units.en: Try writing a micro-version of a story you've read and loved.
units.zh: 尝试为您阅读和喜爱的故事编写微型版本。

units.en: How far can you boil it down without losing the best parts?
units.zh: 在不丢失最好的部分的情况下，您可以将其归结到多远？

units.en: Use a snippet of conversation you have overheard as the starting point for a micro-story.
units.zh: 使用您无意中听到的对话片段作为微故事的起点。

units.en: It could be something youve heard at home, in the street or on a bus.
units.zh: 这可能是您在家中、街上或公共汽车上听到的声音。

units.en: Imagine going on the journey of a lifetime.
units.zh: 想象一下，踏上一生的旅程。

units.en: Who would you take with you?
Where would you go and what would you do when you got there?
units.zh: 你会去哪里，当你到达那里时你会做什么？

units.en: Use a saying or proverb, such as pigs might fly, as the inspiration for a story.
units.zh: 使用一句话或谚语，例如猪可能会飞，作为故事的灵感。

units.en: Think of an intriguing old object you've seen in a shop window or in a museum.
units.zh: 想想你在商店橱窗或博物馆里看到的一个有趣的旧物品。

units.en: Imagine where it might have come from and who once owned it.
units.zh: 想象一下它可能来自哪里以及谁曾经拥有它。

units.en: It's a myth that all great writers were born that way.
units.zh: 这是一个神话，所有伟大的作家都是这样出生的。
